record.original_question: For each class of parameterized benchmark linear systems, develop theoretically and practically fast algorithms.

evidence.quote: For each class of parameterized benchmark linear systems, develop theoretically and practically fast algorithms.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Consider families of linear systems of the form A(p) x = b(p), where p ranges over a parameter domain P (for example a compact subset of R^k) and, for each p in P, A(p) is an n by n real or complex matrix and b(p) is a vector of length n, with the entries of A(p) and b(p) depending on p in a prescribed (e.g. polynomial, rational, or affine) way. Such a family is called a class of parameterized benchmark linear systems. For each natural class of such families (e.g. symmetric positive definite, sparse with banded structure, arising from discretized PDEs, Toeplitz/Hankel, low displacement rank, or affinely parameterized), design an algorithm that, given p in P, returns x(p) satisfying A(p) x(p) = b(p), and that is simultaneously: (i) provably fast, in the sense that its worst-case arithmetic complexity is asymptotically smaller (in n and in the parameter encoding size) than that of a generic dense direct solver, with rigorous error and stability guarantees; and (ii) practically fast, in the sense that an implementation outperforms standard general-purpose solvers on representative benchmark instances of the class. State for which classes such algorithms exist and characterize the achievable complexity.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem as posed is a broad research program rather than a single conjecture, asking for fast solvers for each class of parameterized benchmark linear systems. No single result resolves all classes; while many specific structured classes (e.g. Toeplitz, banded, hierarchical, reduced-basis parametric systems) have efficient solvers, a complete answer covering all benchmark classes is not established.

status_evidence.title: Parameterized linear systems / reduced basis methods
status_evidence.snippet: Open call to develop fast algorithms for each class of parameterized benchmark linear systems.
status_evidence.claim: The question is posed as an open research direction rather than a settled theorem.
